note: The characters who come out of the wave in a city (docs/v2/characters.js), one at a time. The cast: each drawn after one of DIRT's artists, from a species in DIRT's grammar of places, with its plants always the place's own (plants.json). Drawings in scripts/characters/<id>.py; scripts/build_characters.py writes <id>.json. The daily characters pass (REFINE.md) adds one from the backlog and refines the three refined longest ago.

cast.name: Red fox
cast.why: The most widespread wild carnivore on Earth, and a city animal in London, New York, Paris and Melbourne, so it belongs wherever the site's cities are.

after.why: DIRT's ground is drawn after Twombly first (dirt/README.md), and no artist on the roster is nearer a fox among plants: his Natural History portfolios (Mushrooms, 1974; Some Trees of Italy, 1976) are botanical plates. Its coat is in the ochres and rusts of Some Trees of Italy (Title Print), its white in his papers, its black in the Mushrooms' graphite and its outline in their pale grey, a chalk line, as he wrote on his blackboards, so it reads on the city's dark ground; the line it leaves is his writing, in the pale greens of Roman Notes II (light enough to read on the dark ground), a looping pen leaning right, two lines in two inks, lifting between phrases; pressed, it is boxed in red, as he boxed his plates, in the red of Untitled (Roses).
works: Natural History Part II: Some Trees of Italy (Title Print)

cast.poses: trot (four frames, diagonal pairs), stand, back (stops and looks back over its shoulder), look (turned to you), sit
cast.notes: Side on, 40 by 26 cells, two CSS pixels a cell. Guessed still: the trot's knee and hock angles are a two-bone reach, not traced from film; the sitting brush hardly shows round the feet; the turned-back head reads at its size but only just.
log: 2026-10-01 first drawing: three rounds of render and compare (ears restored, legs shortened to a fox's and the body lowered, a fuller brush, a bigger head and longer muzzle, the coat dithered less, the look back lifted clear of the back)

2026-10-01 in the page and the preview: the outline in chalk grey so the black stockings read on the dark city ground, the coat's darkest step kept for the edges between parts (it read as a leopard's spots), no dots small enough to leave gaps; his writing drawn as one continuous looping line behind it

backlog.why: Her Cave paintings after the bison of Lascaux and Altamira (1980s), and the bulls before them; strokes.
Cut shapes: a squirrel leaping the gaps between crowns as a paper cut-out leaps (Jazz, 1947).
Scattered marks: a murmuration is a poured, flung field of dots that turns as one.
A horizon: the Catalan lizard on Dalí's own scrub coast, still on a long flat ground.
Stacked fields: the gorget's colour soaks and floods as it turns, the way her stain soaks the canvas.
Warhol's Endangered Species (1983) has the bald eagle; a grid: seen only as its shadow, repeated.
Dots: points of light in the dark, as his silver prints hold light.
Woldgate Woods and the hawthorn of his garden in DIRT; deer at the edge of an English wood.
Stacked fields of sky: a skein crossing an evening light.
Svayambh (2007): a slow red mass that moves on its own through the place.
The decisive moment: a deer that stops at the edge of the frame and is gone.
